scope: Seed-42 all-layer clipped run and its matched unclipped Experiment 4 run

metric_policy.macro_task_accuracy: Arithmetic mean of KS, SI, and ER accuracies, weighted equally by task.
metric_policy.accuracy_all: Sample-weighted accuracy across all labelled task examples.
metric_policy.test_usage: Test results are descriptive outcomes of validation-selected checkpoints and were not used to select the method.
metric_policy.stability_definition: Optimization stability and row-assignment stability are reported separately.

post_freeze_assignment_match.interpretation: Frozen assignments did not change; the current nearest-pair agreement with those forced assignments gradually declined.

observations: Both clipped and unclipped 100-epoch runs remained numerically stable, so clipping was not necessary for the all-layer configuration.
The clipped run slightly improved validation macro and sample-weighted test accuracy, but reduced descriptive test macro by 0.5506 percentage points because ER decreased by 1.9891 points.
Clipping did not satisfy the adaptive assignment-stability gate and forced assignment freezing at epoch 10, whereas the unclipped baseline naturally stabilized at epoch 4.
The dominant row pair changed from KS-ER without clipping to KS-SI with clipping, demonstrating a material change in the learned sharing structure.
Post-freeze nearest-pair agreement fell to 0.812 by epoch 100; assignments and beta remained frozen, so this is drift relative to the forced epoch-10 structure rather than reassignment.

decision.summary: The 100-epoch result does not justify max_norm=1.0 as the default. Its small weighted-accuracy gain is accompanied by forced row freezing and lower balanced test performance, particularly ER.
decision.reporting_recommendation: Report Experiment 5 as evidence that clipping can prevent catastrophic optimization but can interfere with NCMTL assignment discovery. Retain the unclipped protocol for subsequent primary experiments.
